summary: Meta describes how the University of Pittsburgh's HERL lab and ATDev, under an ARPA-H-funded initiative, are deploying Meta's open-source DINO and SAM vision models on edge devices within the RAMMP assistive mobility robotics platform.

mechanisms.reason: The document describes engineers running DINOv3 and SAM directly on battery-powered edge hardware with reduced memory footprint and lower precision, moving inference off datacentre GPUs onto embedded robotic devices.
mechanisms.quote: Applying both models as part of the development of robotics systems, engineers optimize models for edge devices, reducing memory footprint, using lower precision when appropriate, and deploying in formats tailored for real-world conditions.

practices.reason: Describes concrete edge-deployment optimization tactics (memory reduction, lower precision, format tuning) but tied to the RAMMP team's specific hardware and unreplicated elsewhere.
practices.quote: By running at practical resolutions and with efficient batching, both models stay fast and dependable, even on the compact, battery-powered hardware used in robotic mobility platforms and robotic arms

practices.reason: Describes a concrete pipeline pattern -- using SAM for auto-labeling and DINOv2 embeddings to fine-tune a lightweight RF-DETR detector -- that an engineering team could replicate for perception systems, though results are specific to this project.
practices.quote: By combining SAM's labeling power with DINOv2's rich visual representations in a fine-tuned RF-DETR model, RAMMP achieves real-time 360-degree environmental awareness and adaptive object detection.
